newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor says may tap global markets.
newsitem.headline: Gencor says may tap global markets.

text.p: South African mining house Gencor Ltd said on Monday it was considering accessing international markets to help fund future projects.

"Gencor is currently evaluating a number of major opportunities, including projects in South Africa and Mozambique, in Venezuela and Brazil, and in Colombia and Australia," the company said in a statement.

"Although it is likely that not all of these will advance beyond the study phase, it is clear that Gencor's ability to compete for and finance such projects would be significantly enhanced if it did not have to rely solely on its domestic capital market."

The need to gain access to international capital market, free of capital restrictions, had been a consistent theme of Gencor's reporting to shareholders, the company said following weekend speculation that it was planning to float a new mining group on the London Stock Exchange.
"Gencor is currently investigating a number of transactions that would provide its world-class asset base with such access to the international capital markets," it said.

"Should these transactions prove feasible, they would constitute a major step in re-integrating South African corporates into the mainstream of world capital markets; would be consistent with the government's progressive steps to achieve growth in the economy; would provide our shareholders with enhanced prospects; and would provide new opportunities for our employees, both in South Africa and internationally."
Gencor added that the initiative still had to overcome "a number of hurdles" and had not yet been approved by the board.
"Shareholders are therefore advised to exercise caution their dealings in the company's shares."
Britain's Observer newspaper said on Sunday that Gencor was planning to float a new mining operation in London which could be worth up to one billion pounds ($1.6 billion).

The paper said the new group would be built around mining subsidiary Billiton International and would also embrace large parts of Gencor's non-South African operations which mine gold, platinum, copper, zinc and tin.
It said the flotation was scheduled to take place before the end of the year.
The move would give Gencor a flexible offshore vehicle for the first time and give it a better chance of competing with mahjor players worldwide, the paper said.
